application.answer:
- NVIDIA’s FY2026 revenue, for the year ended January 25, 2026, grew 65% to $215.9 billion. The main driver was Data Center demand as customers shifted toward accelerated computing and AI; Data Center revenue grew 68%. [S9] [S7]

application.answer:
- Intel’s original FY2025 Form 10-K, for the year ended December 27, 2025, describes leading-edge manufacturing process development as risky, capital-intensive and requiring years to generate returns. [S5]

- Development and competitiveness: Intel reports past delays in process technologies and advanced packaging, including performance and yield issues. These allowed competitors using third-party foundries to introduce manufacturing improvements ahead of Intel. [S15]

- Yield and cost: Delayed process introductions can increase die sizes, constrain supply and raise product costs. Lower yields and longer manufacturing times can reduce gross margins. New nodes typically carry higher depreciation and lower yields, and improvements may not match those achieved on earlier nodes. [S12]

- Complexity and defects: Increasing die sizes and transistor counts make processes more susceptible to defects and errata, causing production delays, lower yields and higher manufacturing and warranty costs. Tile-based designs and advanced packaging introduce additional manufacturability risks that could delay competitive products. [S11]

- Intel 14A viability: Without a significant external foundry customer, Intel may pause or discontinue Intel 14A and subsequent leading-edge nodes. Intel reports that it had not secured significant external foundry customers for any node and that Intel 14A customer prospects were uncertain. Discontinuation could be effectively irreversible. [S5] [S6] [S8]

- Financial exposure: Leading-edge facilities require large capital outlays and substantial fixed costs. A potential Intel 14A exit could jeopardize incentives, require repayment of funding and trigger substantial payments under manufacturing investment agreements. [S14] [S10]

- External dependencies: Third-party manufacturing reduces Intel’s control over yields, quality, schedules and costs. ASML is the sole supplier of EUV tools used for specified leading-edge nodes; tool delays could delay future node development or ramps. [S9]
